# Detail-polling layer for in-progress evaluation jobs (Branch A)

## Description

This epic delivers the new detail-polling data layer for the EvalHub Evaluations landing page, built on the assumption (validated by the API behavior investigation of the EvalHub job status endpoints) that the detail endpoint `GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs/{id}` reports per-benchmark progress (`status.benchmarks[]` with `started_at`, `completed_at`, and per-benchmark `status`) while a job is still running. A detail-polling hook identifies which jobs on the currently displayed table page are in a non-terminal state and fetches their detail endpoints on a 10-second cycle to obtain benchmark-level progress data for display, while the existing list endpoint continues its 30-second polling for top-level state. The layer enforces strict client-side load controls: only jobs visible on the current table page are polled, at most 5 requests are in flight at once (round-robin dispatch), and polling pauses when the browser tab is backgrounded. Transient errors are handled with the retry-with-backoff pattern established by the autorag package, preserving the last successful data and surfacing a non-blocking warning.

## Scope

- Build the detail-polling hook that identifies non-terminal jobs among the rows currently displayed on the Evaluations table page (client-side pagination: default 20 rows per page, options 5/10/20) and fetches `GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs/{id}` for each on a 10-second cycle; when all detail fetches for the current page complete, a 10-second timer starts before the next cycle.
- Retarget polling immediately when the table page changes — jobs not in view are not polled; jobs newly in view are polled.
- Enforce the concurrency cap: at most 5 concurrent detail requests per user session, dispatched round-robin (as one request completes, the next pending job is fetched), regardless of how many jobs are running.
- Adopt the autorag React Query polling pattern (`usePipelineRunQuery` in packages/autorag): `placeholderData: (previousData) => previousData` to preserve the last successful response, `retry` with exponential backoff (`RETRY_DELAY_MS * 2^attempt + jitter`, up to MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS), 4xx errors treated as non-retryable, 5xx/network errors retried (up to 5 retries).
- Expose a non-blocking inline warning state (PatternFly Alert variant "warning") indicating that status updates are temporarily unavailable while polling encounters errors, while the last successfully fetched data continues to be displayed; a single failed detail request does not stop the round-robin — partial progress data is acceptable.
- Integrate the Page Visibility API: polling pauses when the browser tab is not in the foreground, resumes when the tab regains focus, and a single polling cycle is triggered immediately on resume.
- Stop polling jobs that reach a terminal state.
- Verify the odh-dashboard BFF proxy transparently passes through all response fields from the eval-hub plugin backend on detail requests (including `status.benchmarks[]` with per-benchmark status and timestamps) — existing behavior, no BFF code change expected.
- Validate the retry pattern in the eval-hub-ui Module Federation context by simulating 5xx errors from the BFF on individual detail endpoints in development (the proxy chain is identical across autorag/automl/eval-hub).
- Ensure requests flow through the existing auth chain unchanged (kube-rbac-proxy sidecar, dashboard backend proxy to the plugin container, `x-forwarded-access-token` forwarding, `X-Tenant` namespace scoping) — no new auth paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Only jobs in a non-terminal state on the currently displayed table page are targeted by detail polling; changing the table page immediately updates which jobs are polled, measured by network requests in browser dev tools matching the visible page's in-progress jobs.
- No more than 5 concurrent detail requests are in flight per user session at any time, measured by browser dev tools; with more than 5 in-progress jobs on the page, requests proceed round-robin until all in-progress jobs on the page have been updated, then a 10-second timer elapses before the next cycle.
- Given the EvalHub Server is temporarily unreachable during detail polling (5xx or network error on a detail fetch), the last successfully fetched benchmark progress for the affected job remains displayed, a non-blocking inline warning is shown, and the round-robin continues with the next in-progress job while the failed request retries with exponential backoff (up to 5 retries), measured by the UI continuing to render stale detail data for the affected job and the warning Alert component being visible.
- Given the user navigates away from the browser tab, detail polling pauses and no further requests are made until the tab regains focus, at which point a single polling cycle is triggered immediately, measured by no network requests to the detail endpoint while the tab is backgrounded (verified via browser dev tools Network tab).
- 4xx responses are not retried; 5xx and network errors are retried with exponential backoff per the autorag pattern, with the last successful response preserved as placeholder data during retries.
- Detail endpoint responses fetched through the BFF proxy include all response fields from the plugin backend (including `status.benchmarks[]` with per-benchmark status and timestamps), verifying transparent passthrough with no BFF code change.
- Until the first detail fetch returns for a given job, the UI shows only the top-level state from the list endpoint for that job (no benchmark progress or elapsed time).
- Polling of a job stops when it reaches a terminal state.
- The retry-with-backoff behavior is validated in the eval-hub-ui Module Federation context by simulating 5xx errors from the BFF on individual detail endpoints in development.

## HLR Traceability

- [P0] HLR1 (detail-polling portion): auto-refresh mechanism using new detail endpoint polling for in-progress job progress on top of the existing list endpoint polling.
- [P0] HLR3: non-blocking error handling during detail polling — last successful state preserved, inline warning displayed, retry with exponential backoff per the autorag pattern.
- [P1] HLR4 (fetch portion): max-5 concurrent round-robin fetch for in-progress jobs on the current table page.
- [P1] HLR6: polling pauses when the browser tab is not in the foreground (Page Visibility API) and resumes immediately on tab focus.

# Benchmark-level progress and elapsed time display (Branch A)

## Description

This epic delivers the progress display for running evaluation jobs in the EvalHub Evaluations landing page table, built on the assumption (validated by the API behavior investigation of the EvalHub job status endpoints) that per-benchmark progress data is available from the detail endpoint while a job is running. For a job with N benchmarks, progress is expressed as "Benchmarks: X/N complete" where X is the count of entries in `status.benchmarks[]` with `status: "completed"`. Elapsed time is computed client-side as the difference between the current time and the earliest `started_at` timestamp across all benchmarks (or `resource.created_at` if no benchmark has started), and displayed alongside the benchmark count. The display consumes the per-job detail data obtained by the detail-polling capability for in-progress jobs on the current table page; until the first detail fetch returns for a given job, the row shows only the top-level state from the list endpoint. Elapsed time serves as the primary progress indicator, with the benchmark count supplementary — mitigating the coarseness of X/N progress for jobs with few benchmarks (e.g., a 1-benchmark job).

## Scope

- Render benchmark-level progress for running jobs as "Benchmarks: X/N complete", where X is the count of `status.benchmarks[]` entries with `status: "completed"` from the job's detail data and N is the total benchmark count for the job.
- Compute and render elapsed time for running jobs client-side: current time minus the earliest per-benchmark `started_at` timestamp in the detail response (falling back to `resource.created_at` when no benchmark has started), displayed in a human-readable form (e.g., "Elapsed: 4m 12s").
- Treat elapsed time as the primary progress indicator for all running jobs, with the benchmark count supplementary, so single-benchmark jobs still convey activity.
- Render per-job progress and elapsed time only after the first successful detail fetch for that job; before that, show only the top-level state from the list endpoint (no benchmark progress or elapsed time).
- Obtain the progress indicator UX specification — the design doc the strategy's Supporting Documentation lists as "to be created" — with authorship owned by UX/Design per the strategy's UXD Support prerequisite ("Required for progress indicator pattern"). This epic's role is to supply the implementation inputs the specification needs (the "Benchmarks: X/N complete" progress model, the elapsed-time computation with its `resource.created_at` fallback, and the data-availability constraints established by the API behavior investigation) and to review the progress display against the authored specification for PatternFly alignment.
- Degrade gracefully: if the detail data is unavailable for a job (detail endpoint unreachable), the row continues to show the last successfully fetched data with the non-blocking warning surfaced by the polling capability, or only top-level state if no detail data was ever fetched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an evaluation job is in the running state with 3 of 5 benchmarks completed, when a user views the Evaluations landing page and the detail-polling cycle has completed for that job, then benchmark-level progress is displayed (e.g., "Benchmarks: 3/5 complete"), measured by the count matching the number of entries in the `status.benchmarks[]` array with `status: "completed"` in the GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs/{id} response.
- Given an evaluation job has been running for 4 minutes, when the detail-polling cycle has fetched the job's detail endpoint, then elapsed time is displayed (e.g., "Elapsed: 4m 12s"), measured by the elapsed time being the difference between the current time and the earliest per-benchmark `started_at` timestamp in the detail response (or `resource.created_at` if no benchmark has started).
- Given a single-benchmark running job, when the row is displayed, then elapsed time is presented as the primary progress indicator with the benchmark count supplementary, measured by the elapsed time rendering being prominent and the benchmark count (0/1 or 1/1) supplementary.
- Given no detail fetch has yet returned for a running job, when the row is displayed, then only the top-level state from the list endpoint is shown — no benchmark progress or elapsed time.
- The progress indicator UX specification is authored by UX/Design (authorship owned by UXD per the strategy's UXD Support prerequisite), and the progress indicator pattern and state treatments are reviewed by UX/Design against that authored specification for PatternFly alignment.

## HLR Traceability

- [P1] HLR4 (display portion): benchmark-level progress display for running jobs (e.g., "Benchmarks: 2/5 complete") derived from the detail endpoint's `status.benchmarks[]` array.
- [P1] HLR5: elapsed time display for running jobs, computed client-side from per-benchmark `started_at` timestamps obtained via detail polling.

# Elapsed-time fallback progress indication (Branch B)

## Description

This epic delivers the fallback progress indication for running evaluation jobs in the EvalHub Evaluations landing page table, built when the API behavior investigation of the EvalHub job status endpoints determines that the detail endpoint's `status.benchmarks[]` array is populated only after job completion — making benchmark-level progress (X/N complete) unavailable mid-run. Per the strategy's pre-specified mitigation, elapsed time becomes the primary progress indicator for all running jobs: the running state with a ticking elapsed-time display provides the feedback the source RFE requires, and overall state continues to come from the existing list endpoint polling and the state differentiation UI. No detail polling of running jobs is built in this outcome, because the detail endpoint provides no mid-run progress data — elapsed time is computed client-side from data already available in the list response.

## Scope

- Compute and render elapsed time for running jobs client-side as the difference between the current time and the job's creation timestamp (`resource.created_at`) from the list endpoint response, displayed in a human-readable form (e.g., "Elapsed: 4m 12s") as the primary progress indicator on the job row.
- Keep elapsed time ticking while the job is in the running state; stop updating when the job reaches a terminal state.
- Where benchmark count data is available from the list response (benchmark config IDs are present in the trimmed list object), it may be shown as supplementary static context; no mid-run per-benchmark progress is displayed because the data does not exist mid-run in this outcome.
- Document the accepted degradation relative to the strategy's benchmark-level progress requirement: benchmark-level progress (X/N) is displayed only where the data supports it, not mid-run.
- Obtain the progress indicator UX specification — the design doc the strategy's Supporting Documentation lists as "to be created" — with authorship owned by UX/Design per the strategy's UXD Support prerequisite ("Required for progress indicator pattern"). This epic's role is to supply the implementation inputs the specification needs (the elapsed-time-as-primary-indicator model computed from `resource.created_at`, the accepted absence of mid-run benchmark progress, and the data-availability constraints established by the API behavior investigation) and to review the elapsed-time display against the authored specification for PatternFly alignment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an evaluation job has been running for 4 minutes, when a user views the Evaluations landing page, then elapsed time is displayed for that job (e.g., "Elapsed: 4m 12s"), measured by the elapsed time being the difference between the current time and the job's `resource.created_at` from the list endpoint response.
- Given a running job, when the row is displayed, then elapsed time is presented as the primary progress indicator, with the overall state badge from the list endpoint — no mid-run benchmark progress is shown.
- Given a job reaches a terminal state (completed/failed), when the row is displayed, then the elapsed-time display stops updating.
- The progress indicator UX specification is authored by UX/Design (authorship owned by UXD per the strategy's UXD Support prerequisite), and the elapsed-time progress indicator pattern is reviewed by UX/Design against that authored specification for PatternFly alignment.
- Implementation confirms `resource.created_at` (or equivalent creation timestamp) is available in the list endpoint response and captures the field used (assumption from the Staff Engineer field inventory: the list object carries core identity including `resource`).

## HLR Traceability

- [P1] HLR5 (fallback variant): elapsed time display for running jobs — computed client-side; in this outcome the data source is the list endpoint's creation timestamp rather than per-benchmark `started_at` from detail polling.
- [P1] HLR4 (degraded): benchmark-level progress display for running jobs is unimplementable mid-run in this outcome; this epic delivers the strategy's pre-specified fallback (elapsed time as primary progress indicator). The degradation is recorded in the decomposition summary's traceability matrix.

# Validate EvalHub job status API behavior for progress display

## Description

This investigation resolves the two open questions that gate the EvalHub evaluation-job progress UI work, by determining what the EvalHub Server's job status APIs actually report while a job is running and when it fails. Both questions are owned by the TrustyAI / EvalHub team per the source strategy and are marked "needs validation" in the strategy's assumptions. The deliverable is a written determination, with evidence, that selects which progress-display approach is built and which failure-distinction variant the state UI renders.

The questions:

1. Is `status.benchmarks[]` in the `GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs/{id}` (detail) response populated with per-benchmark status entries (`started_at`, `completed_at`, per-benchmark `status`) while a job is still running, or only after completion? If only populated on completion, benchmark-level progress (X/N complete) is unavailable mid-run and the UI can only show elapsed time plus overall state.
2. What values does `status.message.message_code` take for pre-start failures (admission error, resource quota, scheduling failure) versus runtime failures? This determines whether the UI can reliably distinguish "Failed (not started)" from "Failed" (runtime).

Per Staff Engineer direction, the UI must assume no data beyond what the two existing endpoints (list `GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs` and detail `GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs/{id}`) already provide, so the answers bound what the frontend can display.

## Scope

- Inspect the published EvalHub Server API reference (GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs and GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs/{id}) and the EvalHub Server source code to determine when per-benchmark status entries are appended to `status.benchmarks[]` (during execution vs. at completion) and what fields each entry carries mid-run.
- Enumerate the `message_code` values the EvalHub Server emits for failure paths, classifying which indicate pre-start failures (admission, scheduling, resource quota) versus runtime failures, and assess whether they reliably distinguish the two classes across error scenarios.
- If source and docs are inconclusive, validate empirically: exercise a running evaluation job (EvalHub Server local/development mode, or a development cluster) and capture an observed mid-run detail response for a multi-benchmark job, plus failure responses for a pre-start failure scenario.
- Record the outcome so that: (a) the progress-display approach is selected — benchmark-level progress from detail polling versus the elapsed-time-only fallback computed from list-endpoint data; and (b) the failure-distinction variant is chosen for the state UI — two failure states versus the fallback single "Failed" state with `status.message.message` text as supplementary detail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written determination states whether `status.benchmarks[]` is populated while a job is running or only after completion, citing evidence (API reference section, source location, or an observed captured response).
- A written enumeration of `status.message.message_code` values for pre-start versus runtime failures, with a conclusion on whether they reliably distinguish the two classes (pass: at least admission/scheduling/quota codes distinguishable from runtime codes; fail: ambiguous or absent — fallback applies).
- If empirical validation was needed, the method is documented (local dev mode or development cluster) and the captured mid-run response is attached to the determination.
- The determination is delivered to the ODH Dashboard implementation team in time to select the progress-display approach and failure-distinction variant before implementation of the polling and display work begins.

## HLR Traceability

- Enables [P0] HLR1 (auto-refresh with detail polling for in-progress job progress) — the answer determines whether the detail-polling layer is built.
- Enables [P1] HLR4 (benchmark-level progress display) and [P1] HLR5 (elapsed time display) — the answer selects the data source and display shape.
- Enables [P2] HLR7 (pre-start vs. runtime failure distinction) — the message_code answer selects the failure-distinction variant and its fallback.

# Evaluations table state differentiation and failure distinction UI

## Description

This epic delivers the visual state differentiation for evaluation jobs in the EvalHub Evaluations landing page table, driven entirely by the list endpoint (`GET /api/v1/evaluations/jobs`) data that the page already fetches with its existing 30-second polling. Each job row gets a distinct PatternFly status treatment — icon, color, and label — for queued/pending, running, failed, and completed states, derived from the `status.state` field available for all jobs without any detail fetch. Failed rows surface `status.message` as error context. The epic also implements the pre-start versus runtime failure distinction using `status.message.message_code` where the available values support it, falling back to a single "Failed" state with the message text as supplementary detail when the code is ambiguous or absent. State transitions (pending → running → complete/failed) become visible without manual browser refresh as the existing list polling refreshes the table.

## Scope

- Map `status.state` values from the list endpoint to four distinct visual states in the job table: Queued/Pending, Running, Failed, Completed — each with a distinct PatternFly status icon, color, and label text per the PatternFly status pattern.
- Render `status.message` as error context on failed job rows.
- Implement the pre-start vs. runtime failure distinction: where `status.message.message_code` indicates an admission error, scheduling failure, or resource constraint, render "Failed (not started)"; runtime errors render "Failed". This requires no new API state enum values.
- Apply the pre-specified fallback when `message_code` values do not distinguish failure classes (or are absent): a single "Failed" state with `status.message.message` text displayed as supplementary detail. The variant to build is selected by the API behavior validation of the EvalHub job status endpoints.
- Ensure the job table row state label updates automatically within the existing list polling interval (30 seconds) as jobs transition states — no manual page refresh required.
- Obtain UX/Design review of the state icon and color specifications and PatternFly alignment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an evaluation job is queued/pending (not yet started), when a user views the Evaluations landing page, then the job row displays a distinct "Queued" label and visual treatment distinguishable from "Running" and "Failed" states, measured by distinct icon, color, and label text per the PatternFly status pattern.
- Given an evaluation job transitions from running to complete, when the user is on the Evaluations landing page without manually refreshing the browser, then the status update is visible within the list endpoint's polling interval (30 seconds), measured by the job list row updating its state label automatically.
- Given an evaluation job failed before execution started (e.g., admission error indicated by `status.message.message_code`), when a user views the Evaluations landing page, then the job row displays a distinct visual treatment differentiating it from a job that ran and then failed, measured by a label reflecting the failure type and an icon/color distinct from the runtime "Failed" state.
- Given `status.message.message_code` is ambiguous or absent for a failed job, when a user views the row, then a single "Failed" state renders with `status.message.message` text as supplementary detail (fallback behavior).
- State icon and color specifications are reviewed and approved by UX/Design against the dashboard design system and PatternFly status pattern.

## HLR Traceability

- [P0] HLR2: Visual distinction between queued/pending, actively running, failed, and completed states with distinct labels, icons, and color treatments derived from the list endpoint's `status.state` field.
- [P2] HLR7: Pre-start vs. runtime failure distinction using `status.message.message_code` where available (bundled here rather than split — it renders in the same status-column UI surface as the P0 state work; the fallback variant is pre-specified in the strategy).
- [P0] HLR1 (partial): top-level state transitions shown without manual refresh via the existing list endpoint polling.
